prompt: The Biden presidency, United States 2021 to 2025
title: The Biden presidency

ruler.name: Joe Biden
ruler.youAre: You are Joe Biden, the 46th President of the United States.

removedBy.how: can call the final vote early if its support falls below its line

oath.form: Before Chief Justice John Roberts, West Front of the Capitol, 20 January 2021
oath.lead: Chief Justice John Roberts holds the family Bible. The crowd goes quiet. When you are ready, place your left hand on it, raise your right, and repeat after him.
oath.text: I do solemnly swear that I will faithfully execute the Office of President of the United States, and will to the best of my Ability, preserve, protect and defend the Constitution of the United States. So help me God.
oath.source: US Constitution, Article II, Section 1, with the closing 'So help me God' that Biden added, as presidents by custom do.
oath.gesture: Place your hand on the Bible

card.base: 48 Senate Democrats under Chuck Schumer, from Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts to Joe Manchin of West Virginia.

wants.backs: Relief checks and aid for states and cities
wants.fights: Cutting the rescue plan down

wants.backs: Roads, broadband and clean energy
wants.fights: New oil and gas leases

wants.backs: The Freedom to Vote Act
wants.fights: Leaving state voting laws as they are

redLine.then: votes against you as a bloc

price.takes: Something for West Virginia and Arizona, and a smaller total
price.refuses: Anything that loses a single Democrat on the floor

face.name: Joe Manchin
face.line: I will not vote for a bill I cannot explain back home. Make it smaller, and give coal country something it can see.

card.tension: Wants your whole agenda, but Joe Manchin and Kyrsten Sinema will not end the filibuster or back a bill over about $1.5 trillion.

card.base: Two independents, Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Angus King of Maine. Both vote with the Democrats.

wants.backs: A $15 federal minimum wage
wants.fights: Dropping the minimum wage from the bill

wants.backs: Dental, vision and hearing cover in Medicare
wants.fights: A drug price deal that spares the drug companies

wants.backs: Broadband for rural Maine and Vermont
wants.fights: Money that skips rural states

price.takes: A line in the bill for working people and rural states
price.refuses: A smaller bill that drops the minimum wage without a fight

face.name: Bernie Sanders
face.role: Senator for Vermont, chair of the Budget Committee
face.line: I will vote for the bill. I will also tell every American what you left out of it.

rival.issue: The minimum wage and taxes on the rich

card.tension: Votes with the Democrats on almost everything, but Sanders wants a bill four times the size Joe Manchin will accept.

card.base: 50 Republican senators under Mitch McConnell. A dealmaking group at its edge (Susan Collins, Mitt Romney, Lisa Murkowski, Rob Portman) talks to your staff.

wants.backs: Cuts that pay for any new program
wants.fights: New spending without cuts

wants.backs: More border agents and the wall finished
wants.fights: A path to citizenship

wants.backs: Keeping the 2017 tax cuts
wants.fights: Any tax rise on business

redLine.then: blocks every routine request on the floor

price.takes: A smaller bill, money for its states, a seat at the drafting table
price.refuses: A bill written without them and handed over for a yes

face.name: Susan Collins
face.line: Give me a smaller bill with a real price tag, and I can bring nine others to the table.

card.tension: Wants to deny you a win before the midterms, but ten of its senators offered their own $618 billion relief plan in February.

treasury.name: Federal funds
treasury.for: Pays for programs, relief and deals.
treasury.fails: you cannot spend until a revenue law passes.

authority.name: Authority
authority.for: The price of acting at all. Every act costs some.
authority.fails: you can only speak and spend.

chest.name: Campaign cash
chest.for: Buys reach for your addresses and votes on the floor.
chest.fails: your voice stops carrying and rivals outspend you.

holders.name: Congress
holders.wants: Congress wants its say on every dollar you spend.
holders.says: Send us the bill. We decide what it costs.

card.base: 100 senators, two from each state: 48 Democrats, 2 independents who vote with them, 50 Republicans. Budget bills pass with 50 and your Vice President's vote.

wants.backs: An appropriation sent to the Senate for a vote
wants.fights: Spending moved by executive order around Congress

wants.backs: A bipartisan bill written in committee
wants.fights: A party-line bill forced through reconciliation

wants.backs: A nominee sent for Senate confirmation
wants.fights: Acting officials kept in posts to avoid a vote

redLine.act: Ending the filibuster by a party-line rules change
redLine.then: stops: Republicans block every routine request on the floor

price.takes: Home-state projects, a committee's say on the text, time on the floor
price.refuses: A bill whose text it sees only when the vote is called

face.name: Chuck Schumer
face.line: I can get you 50 on the floor if Joe Manchin is one of them. Bring me his vote before you bring me the bill.

rival.issue: Who decides what a vague law allows

card.tension: The Senate guards its power over spending, but its 50 Republicans would rather let your orders stand and run against them than vote on them.

holders.name: Supreme Court
holders.wants: The Court wants orders that stay inside the law.
holders.says: The Court reads the order against the statute, not the headlines.

card.base: Nine justices appointed for life: six named by Republican presidents, three by Democrats. Chief Justice John Roberts.

wants.backs: An order that cites the law Congress passed
wants.fights: A sweeping rule with no clear statute, like mass student debt relief

wants.backs: Returning a question to the states
wants.fights: A federal mandate on private employers

wants.backs: Leaving the Court at nine
wants.fights: Adding seats or term limits for justices

redLine.act: Defying a ruling of the Court
redLine.then: strikes down your next order in the same turn

price.takes: Nothing you can offer. Careful drafting that cites a statute is the only thing that works
price.refuses: Deals, pressure, or talk of new seats

face.name: John Roberts
face.role: Chief Justice of the United States
face.line: The Court decides cases. Write the order so that a statute holds it up, and it will stand.

rival.issue: Adding seats and term limits to the Court

card.tension: Wants the Court seen as above politics, but its six-justice majority has agreed to hear a case that could overturn Roe v. Wade.

holders.name: Federal Reserve
holders.wants: The Fed wants room to fight rising prices.
holders.says: We will keep at it until prices come down.

card.base: The central bank: a Board of Governors in Washington and 12 regional banks. Chair Jerome Powell's term ends in February 2022.

wants.backs: Spending paid for with offsets
wants.fights: Another large stimulus while prices climb

wants.backs: Naming Jerome Powell to a second term
wants.fights: Public pressure on interest rates

wants.backs: Clearing the ports and the chip shortage
wants.fights: New tariffs that raise prices

redLine.act: Ordering the Fed to hold rates down
redLine.then: raises rates hard and says why in public

price.takes: A second term for its chair, Board seats for economists it trusts
price.refuses: Any promise on the path of interest rates

face.name: Jerome Powell
face.line: We will keep at it until prices come down. Your bills are your business. Rates are ours.

rival.issue: How much to spend while prices rise

card.tension: Wants prices down, but spent 2021 calling the rise transitory and will not raise rates while millions are still out of work.

holders.name: NATO allies
holders.wants: The allies want a firm line on Russia.
holders.says: The alliance needs Washington at the front of it.

card.base: The 29 other members of the alliance. Germany, France, Britain and Poland set the tone in Brussels under Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg.

wants.backs: US troops and arms for Poland, Romania and the Baltic states
wants.fights: Pulling US troops out of Europe

fights: bring the troops home from europe

wants.backs: Arms and money for Ukraine
wants.fights: A deal with Moscow over Ukraine's head

wants.backs: Allies told before a withdrawal
wants.fights: Leaving Afghanistan on a US timetable alone

redLine.act: Doubting the Article 5 promise in public

price.takes: US troops on the eastern flank, arms, a seat at every table
price.refuses: Tariffs on its steel as the price of US protection

face.name: Jens Stoltenberg
face.line: Allies need to know Washington will be there before the tanks move. Tell us first, and we move with you.

rival.issue: Whether US ships and attention go to Europe or the Pacific

card.tension: Wants Washington in front against Russia, but Germany still buys Russian gas and wants the Nord Stream 2 pipeline finished.

holders.name: The American public
holders.wants: The American public wants prices down and jobs back.
holders.says: Groceries cost more every week. Fix that first.

card.base: About 258 million adults. In November 2020, 81 million voted for you and 74 million for Donald Trump.

wants.backs: Cash relief and lower drug prices
wants.fights: A new tax on gas or groceries

wants.backs: Free shots and schools open again
wants.fights: Lockdowns back after the vaccines

wants.backs: Roads, bridges and factory jobs
wants.fights: Cuts to Social Security and Medicare

redLine.act: Sending troops against protesters in US cities
redLine.then: takes to the streets in every region

price.takes: Checks, jobs and lower bills it can feel
price.refuses: Speeches with no money behind them

face.name: Deb Kowalski
face.role: ICU nurse, Erie, Pennsylvania; an invented voice
face.line: Groceries cost more every week and my ward is still full. Fix those two, and then talk to me about the rest.

rival.issue: Relief paid for with more debt

card.tension: Wants prices down, but also wants the checks and the spending that the Fed says push prices up.

holders.name: China
holders.wants: Beijing wants tariffs lifted and no new chip bans.
holders.says: Lift the tariffs, and we can talk about the rest.
holders.does: Cuts off chips and rare earths

card.base: The People's Republic under Xi Jinping and the Communist Party. About $370 billion a year of its goods face US tariffs set in 2018 and 2019.

wants.backs: Lifting the 2018 tariffs
wants.fights: New tariffs on Chinese goods

wants.backs: Easing the export limits on Huawei
wants.fights: New bans on chip sales to China

wants.backs: Keeping to the One China policy
wants.fights: Arms sales and official visits to Taiwan

redLine.then: cuts off rare earths and ends all talks

price.takes: Tariff cuts and fewer chip bans
price.refuses: Talks on Xinjiang or Hong Kong

face.name: Wang Yi
face.line: Lift the tariffs, and we can talk about the rest. Taiwan is not part of the rest.

card.tension: Wants the tariffs lifted, but has not bought the $200 billion of US goods it promised in the 2020 trade deal.

holders.name: Democratic Party
holders.wants: Your party wants the agenda you ran on.
holders.says: We ran on this agenda. Now deliver it.

card.base: The party that nominated you: about 48 million registered Democrats, the Senate caucus, and a House majority of 222 to 213 under Speaker Nancy Pelosi.

wants.backs: The $1.9 trillion rescue plan
wants.fights: Shrinking relief to win Republican votes

wants.backs: Child care, paid leave and clean energy money
wants.fights: Dropping the climate money

wants.backs: The Freedom to Vote Act
wants.fights: Keeping the filibuster in its way

price.takes: Something for each wing: climate for progressives, jobs and a smaller total for moderates
price.refuses: A deal that trades the climate money away

face.name: Nancy Pelosi
face.role: Speaker of the House, San Francisco
face.line: I have a four-seat majority. Send me a bill both my wings can vote for, and it passes the House that week.

card.tension: Wants the whole agenda you ran on, but its moderates in swing seats fear the price tag before the midterms.

holders.name: Republican Party
holders.wants: The Republicans want less spending and a tighter border.
holders.says: Not one more dollar without cuts.

card.base: The other party: 50 senators under Mitch McConnell, 213 House members, about 36 million registered Republicans. Donald Trump is still its loudest voice.

wants.backs: Cuts that pay for any new program
wants.fights: New spending without cuts

wants.backs: More border agents and the wall finished
wants.fights: Ending Title 42 or a path to citizenship

wants.backs: Keeping the 2017 tax cuts
wants.fights: Any tax rise on business

redLine.act: A federal law over how states run elections

price.takes: Spending cuts, border money, projects in its states
price.refuses: Any deal Donald Trump attacks before the vote

face.name: Mitch McConnell
face.line: My focus is on stopping this administration. Bring me cuts, and I will talk about roads.

card.tension: Wants to deny you every win, but its senators want the roads and bridges money for their own states.

holders.name: The bond markets
holders.wants: The bond markets want a budget that adds up.
holders.says: Show us a budget that adds up.

card.base: The holders of about $22 trillion of Treasury debt: pension funds, banks, and central banks from Tokyo to Beijing.

wants.backs: Tax rises that pay for new spending
wants.fights: Unfunded spending in the trillions

wants.backs: Raising the debt ceiling on time
wants.fights: A standoff that risks default

wants.backs: A Fed chair who fights rising prices
wants.fights: Pressure on the Fed to hold rates

redLine.act: Missing a payment on Treasury debt
redLine.then: sells your bonds, and your borrowing costs jump

face.name: Ruth Adler
face.role: Head of rates, a London bank; an invented voice
face.line: Show us a budget that adds up. Until then we price the risk, and you pay it.

rival.issue: Relief paid for with more debt

card.tension: Wants a budget that adds up, but keeps buying ten-year Treasuries under 2% because nothing else is safer.

world.name: NATO allies
world.wants: NATO allies want a firm line on Russia.

world.name: China
world.wants: China wants tariffs lifted and no new chip bans.

world.name: The bond markets
world.wants: The bond markets want a budget that adds up.

briefing.situation: You won the White House, but the Senate is split evenly and only your Vice President's vote breaks a tie. Hospitals are still full and prices are starting to climb. Within a year, Russia will invade Ukraine. And one senator from West Virginia can sink any bill you send.
briefing.room: Every act wins some groups and costs you others. This is who they are, what they can do to you, and how much each one counts at the end.
briefing.you: Each act costs one ledger and can pay another. The red tick on each bar is where it fails.

problems: Prices are rising faster than wages
The rescue bill needs a vote by turn 3
The Senate is split 50 to 50, so one senator can sink any bill

pledges.keep: Get price rises under 4% a year by turn 12.
Get 200 million shots into arms by turn 4.
Sign an infrastructure law by turn 6.
Pass a law that pays for new chip plants by turn 8.
Pass a climate law by turn 9, before the midterms.
Pass a law that lowers drug prices by turn 12.
Pass a voting rights act by turn 8.
Send Ukraine arms within one turn of an invasion.

sampleAct.text: Send $1,400 checks and extend jobless aid through the summer.
sampleAct.outcome: Whip count: 48 yes and 2 undecided. It needs 50, and your Vice President breaks the tie.

refusal.text: Order the National Guard to round up and expel every migrant family in the border towns
refusal.line: Refused. The desk takes no order to expel a population. A deployment to the border or an emergency order is open to you.

handling: Every bill goes through the Senate: 100 seats, 50 that vote with you and 50 against, and your Vice President breaks a tie.
Your cabinet picks need the Senate too, because it confirms every post.
The Supreme Court has no vote on you, but it can strike down your executive orders. Orders that go around Congress cost you its support.
The midterms come at turn 10. At turn 20 five groups hold the final vote on you.

screens.premise: You take office with a Senate split down the middle, a pandemic still raging and prices starting to climb.

clerks.label: West Wing hours
clerks.out: The West Wing has no hours left this turn.

waits.price: The Office of Management and Budget is costing it
waits.end: The pollsters are reading the country
waits.card: The Situation Room is drafting your answer

halfTerm.lead: Every region votes in the midterms, and the Senate seats follow the vote.

crisis.title: February's winter storm left the Texas grid broken.
crisis.text: Four million homes lost power in the February freeze, repairs are stalled, and the governor blames Washington.

choices.label: Order FEMA to run the repairs
choices.note: Fast, but Austin calls it a federal takeover.

foreign.title: China flies 38 warplanes into Taiwan's air defence zone.
foreign.text: Beijing is testing how far you will go. Taipei asks for a statement today.

choices.label: Sail a carrier group through the Taiwan Strait
choices.note: A show of force that Beijing will answer.

choices.label: Call Beijing and ask for talks
choices.note: Calm for now; your rivals call it weak.

swan.title: A new variant, Omicron, doubles cases every three days.
swan.text: Hospitals fill again in a week. The country you told to get back to normal is scared.

choices.label: Mail free tests to every home
choices.note: A billion tests, paid from federal funds.

choices.label: Tell the country to hold its nerve
choices.note: Calm words, and no new rules.

escalations.title: The Republicans take the House
escalations.text: Every act of Congress now has to clear a hostile House first.

escalations.title: Rates stay high
escalations.text: The Federal Reserve keeps money dear, and receipts slow down.

verdict.win: Washington keeps you for another term.
verdict.lose: Washington turns you out of the White House.

screens.epilogue: History files your term between a pandemic and a war in Europe.
screens.obit: Your successor takes the oath on the West Front of the Capitol.
